defect: three bars occupy roughly square footprint but text glyphs dominate the full lockup crop; mark alone is not always centered in avatar viewport
6 bars at strokeWeight=1 and spacing=0.15 are thin and tightly packed; individual bars may blur into a grey block at 16px
suggested_fix: favour this candidate at 32px and above; mark detail lost below that

defect: dense 6-bar silhouette fills crop but is less immediately distinctive than 3-bar variants
3 steps with wide rounded corners reads as generic progress-bar or loading indicator; risks overlap with common UI component language rather than a distinct brand mark
suggested_fix: consider sharper corners or asymmetric proportions to increase distinctiveness

defect: 6 steps at stepWidth=0.18 produce very fine columns (7.2px each); at 16px the columns may merge into a single featureless band
suggested_fix: use at 32px+ only; below that visual weight is too fine

defect: six fine columns at 16px in avatar crop produce a near-indistinct rectangular mass
3 arcs at strokeWidth=2 with staggered offset; at 16px the arcs are thin enough to lose individual ring distinctiveness and read as a noisy arc cluster
suggested_fix: strokeWidth 2.5+ would improve ring visibility at favicon scale

defect: three staggered arcs produce an open/unbalanced silhouette in a tight circle crop; mark reads as asymmetric noise rather than a coherent symbol
suggested_fix: tighter radii spread or increased stroke weight would improve crop legibility

defect: two concentric arcs with 270° sweep and no offset reads as a loading spinner or progress ring — very common UI metaphor; risks being read as a loading state rather than a brand mark
suggested_fix: consider rotation offset or a third arc to differentiate from progress-circle tropes

defect: 3 arcs at strokeWidth=2.5 with generous radii spread; the outermost arc occupies the full 40px bounding box while innermost is 6px radius — at 16px the inner arc may be invisible
suggested_fix: reduce radiiSpread or increase inner arc radius for favicon scale

defect: the wide radii spread means the inner arc may be too small to read in a 96×96 circle crop
2 arcs at strokeWidth=2 with wide radii gap (radiiSpread=0.4); at 16px the inner arc's radius is very small (6px) and the stroke may not render visibly
suggested_fix: increase strokeWidth to 2.5+ or reduce radiiSpread for favicon scale

defect: two arcs with very wide gap; inner arc is small in the crop viewport
typemark is entire 'accrue' wordmark with cc-echo at opacity=0.35; at 16px the letterforms are below readable size and the echo effect merges with primary glyphs
suggested_fix: Direction D candidates are lockup-only marks; 16px favicon should show mark-only variant; echo dx/dy=4 at favicon scale is imperceptible

defect: cc-echo uses opacity=0.35 which produces a grey ghost; in monochrome this reduces to a lighter-grey duplicate that may lack sufficient contrast from background
suggested_fix: use opacity >= 0.5 or switch to a stroked echo for better monochrome contrast

defect: the full typemark 'accrue' in a circle crop results in very small letterforms and the echo effect is essentially invisible in a 96px diameter viewport
suggested_fix: crop should show only the 'cc' portion for avatar use

defect: all-three motifs: cc echo + stepped-e crossbar + u fill-interval; at 16px the combined motif density makes the letterforms indistinct; stepDepth=24 and fillColor=#E9EEF2 (Fog) contribute low-contrast fill on light background
suggested_fix: Fog fill (#E9EEF2) on Paper (#FAFBFC) background produces very low contrast at small sizes

defect: fillColor=#E9EEF2 (Fog) renders as near-white in monochrome context — the u-fill interval detail is lost entirely; the stepped-e crossbar may also be too fine to survive monochrome at small size
suggested_fix: replace Fog fill with a mid-grey (#AAAAAA or similar) for monochrome-safe operation; or remove the fill interval detail entirely

defect: full typemark in avatar crop; detail density is high and individual motifs (echo+stepped+fill) compound into visual noise at 96px
